name: Iridium
what_failed: 66-satellite global phone network. Bankrupt within a year of launch. Later resurrected for niche use.
why_it_failed: Cellular networks expanded faster than expected
Target market (global business travelers) was too small
Technology was impressive but economically unviable
assumptions_that_broke: Business travelers would pay premium for global coverage
Satellite phones would be primary devices
constraints_that_moved: Roaming agreements reduced need for satellite
IoT created new satellite use cases
resurrection_conditions: IoT and M2M communications (not consumer voice)
lesson: A technology that is correct about the problem but wrong about the timing and the market will fail. Iridium was right about global coverage, wrong about who would pay for it. Resurrected when the market changed.
